subject: Orion Bio trial: prompt set & eval data request
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Patel <aisha@orionbio.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-30T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: trial scope + prompt/log request

Thanks again for the time today — useful call. Summarizing the plan and immediate asks so we have a single source of truth. Quick TL;DR: Redwood will run a contra/baseline eval on the prompts/logs you provide and deliver a short results deck + recommended configuration for the trial by June 14.

Key success criteria (from our conversation):
- End-user intent classification accuracy >= 90% on your high-priority flows (billing, clinical-query, order-status)
- Latency: 99th percentile generation latency < 250ms for 0–512 token responses under the trial load
- Failure modes: no more than 1% hallucination rate on a sampled eval set (we'll define exact scoring below)

Evaluation plan we propose:
1) You provide: a) representative prompt set (user requests) + b) anonymized logs with ground-truth labels where available. See file checklist below.
2) Redwood runs the eval on the candidate model(s) and our recommended quantization profile; we produce: accuracy/precision/recall by intent, latency percentiles, token cost estimates, and example outputs for manual review.
3) Joint review call to agree on pass/fail and narrow the pilot config; if pass, we move to a 2-week ramped trial with dedicated capacity.

Timeline (flexible):
- Please share sample prompts + descriptor by EOD 2026-06-01 (this week)
- Redwood returns initial eval results by 2026-06-14
- Joint review + next-step decision by 2026-06-16

Ownership:
- Orion: deliver prompt/log files and data descriptor (Aisha)
- Redwood: run eval and deliver results (Marcus), SRE/solutions support (Lauren + Stephanie)

Required files (what we need to run the eval):
- prompt set (JSONL): one line per user prompt, include "flow" label where possible
- logs export (JSONL or CSV): timestamped requests, model outputs, user_id (hashed), and ground-truth label if available
- data_descriptor.xlsx: column descriptions and any redaction rules applied

Attachments (what to attach on your side): we will accept obfuscated logs; please include a short note if any fields were dropped. If you prefer, we can provide a template.

Next steps for this thread: please reply with the files or a link to a secure share. If you need a quick template, I can drop one in Drive right now (cc'ing Lauren to prepare).

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

--
Marcus Lin

Marcus — thanks for the clear summary. Attaching an initial drop: two files (see attachment stubs below). We scrubbed PII and hashed user IDs. A few notes:
- The logs are sampled from the last 30 days and skew toward our high-traffic billing and clinical flows. We included an intent column where we have labels.
- We don't have ground truth for ~40% of the clinical queries (no manual labels) — happy for Redwood to run a human-in-the-loop for those or to suggest sampling.

Attachments (attached to this reply):
- orion_prompt_logs_20260530.jsonl (sampled prompts + model outputs; ~4,200 lines)
- orion_data_descriptor_20260530.xlsx (column descriptions & redaction notes)

Questions:
1) For the hallucination metric, can you propose a short annotation rubric we can use to bootstrap labels?
2) Does Redwood need raw audio transcripts for any voice flows? Not for this pilot — we have text only.

We'll aim to push a larger export by 2026-06-05 if that helps.

Thanks,
Aisha

Subject: Re: Post-call: trial scope + prompt/log request

Got the files — thanks, Aisha. Lauren and Stephanie, thanks for standing by. Quick responses to Aisha's questions and our proposed acceptance thresholds:

1) Annotation rubric for hallucination (short):
- 0 = Correct/Supported: model output is supported by input context or ground-truth
- 1 = Minor Fabrication: adds a small unsupported detail that doesn't change intent
- 2 = Hallucination: invents incorrect facts that would materially mislead a user
We can provide a 30-row annotation sheet and have your SMEs label a small sample; Redwood will calculate sample-level hallucination rate and surface examples.

2) Audio transcripts not needed for this trial — text only is fine.

Proposed pass/fail thresholds (for discussion):
- Intent classification accuracy >= 90% on annotated sample
- Hallucination rate <= 1.0% on sampled outputs labeled by SMEs
- 99th pct latency < 250ms on recommended infra for 95% of sample queries

Operational ask: If you can provide a Drive link or SFTP to the full export by 2026-06-05, we will queue the run and aim to return the initial eval by 2026-06-14.

HubSpot note: I updated the deal with the file names above and added our proposed acceptance thresholds (link: https://hubspot.redwood.example/deal/RD-3421-OB).

Next call suggestion: a 30-min checkpoint on 2026-06-10 to review initial anomalies and align on the annotation sample. Does 10:00am PT work for you?

--
Marcus

Thanks — this looks good. A couple clarifications from our side:
- For clinical queries, we'd prefer recall over precision (we're OK with a slightly higher false positive rate if recall improves). Can Redwood include per-intent precision/recall breakdowns so we can tune the threshold per-flow?
- Procurement: if the trial demonstrates clear savings, what's the earliest we can get a Dedicated capacity quote? We're talking to procurement but wanted to prep an ask.

We can provide an expanded export by 2026-06-05. Also happy to have a 10am PT 2026-06-10 checkpoint.

Tom
VP Engineering, Orion Bio

- Redwood provides: initial eval deck (accuracy, precision/recall by intent, latency percentiles, cost estimates, and example outputs) by 2026-06-14 (Marcus, Lauren)

Procurement note: we can share a Dedicated capacity starter quote within 48 hours of the June 14 results if the pilot looks promising — I'll loop in our commercial lead on that path after the review call.

Action items (owners):

If anything changes on timing please flag it on this thread. Appreciate the quick turnaround — we will treat this as high priority.

Thanks — talk next week.
